Not Enrolled? Sign Up Now. Loading Loading Loading Loading Loading Loading Loading Checking Accounts Choose the checking account that works best for you. See our Chase Total Checking ® offer for new customers. Make purchases with your debit card, and bank from almost anywhere by phone, tablet or computer and more than 14,000 ATMs and 5,000 branches. Savings Accounts & CDs It’s never too early to begin saving. Open a savings account or open a Certificate of Deposit ( see interest rates ) and start saving your money. Credit Cards Chase credit cards can help you buy the things you need. Many of our cards offer rewards that can be redeemed for cash back or travel-related perks. With so many options, it can be easy to find a card that matches your lifestyle. Plus, with Credit Journey you can get a free credit score ! Mortgages & Home Equity Buy a home , refinance or put your home's equity to work with a cash-out refinance or home equity line of credit (HELOC) . View today's mortgage rates , use our mortgage calculator , and visit our Education Center for helpful tips. Start your mortgage preapproval online. Auto Chase Auto is here to help you get the right car. Apply for auto financing for a new or used car with Chase. Use the payment calculator to estimate monthly payments. Check out the Chase Auto Education Center to get car guidance from a trusted source. Chase for Business With Chase for Business you’ll receive all-in-one services and guidance from a team of business professionals. Explore business checking , simplify payments acceptance with merchant services , and consider small business loans or business credit cards for help with growth. You can also visit our business resource center . Sports & Entertainment Chase gives you access to unique sports, entertainment and culinary events through Chase Experiences and our exclusive partnerships such as the US Open , Madison Square Garden and Chase Center . Chase Security Center Our suite of security features can help you protect your info, money and give you peace of mind. See how we're dedicated to helping protect you , your accounts and your loved ones from financial abuse . Also, learn about the common tricks scammers are using to help you stay one step ahead of them. If you see unauthorized charges or believe your account was compromised contact us right away to report fraud . About Chase Chase serves millions of people with a broad range of products. Chase online lets you manage your Chase accounts, view statements, monitor activity, pay bills or transfer funds securely from one central place. To learn more, visit the Banking Education Center . For questions or concerns, please contact Chase customer service or let us know about Chase complaints and feedback . View the Chase Community Reinvestment Act Public File for the bank’s latest CRA rating and other CRA-related information. Investing by J.P. Morgan Partner with a global leader who puts your financial needs first. Invest on your own or work with an advisor — we have the products , technology and investment education , to help you grow your wealth. Visit a J.P. Morgan Wealth Management Branch or check out our latest online investing features , offers, promotions, and coupons . Checking Accounts

Choose the checking account that works best for you. See our Chase Total Checking® offer for new customers. Make purchases with your debit card, and bank from almost anywhere by phone, tablet or computer and more than 14,000 ATMs and 5,000 branches.

Savings Accounts & CDs

It’s never too early to begin saving. Open a savings account or open a Certificate of Deposit (see interest rates) and start saving your money.

Credit Cards

Chase credit cards can help you buy the things you need. Many of our cards offer rewards that can be redeemed for cash back or travel-related perks. With so many options, it can be easy to find a card that matches your lifestyle. Plus, with Credit Journey you can get a free credit score!

Mortgages

Apply for a mortgage or refinance your mortgage with Chase. View today’s mortgage rates or calculate what you can afford with our mortgage calculator. Visit our Education Center for homebuying tips and more.

Auto

Chase Auto is here to help you get the right car. Apply for auto financing for a new or used car with Chase. Use the payment calculator to estimate monthly payments. Check out the Chase Auto Education Center to get car guidance from a trusted source.

Chase for Business

With Chase for Business you’ll receive guidance from a team of business professionals who specialize in helping improve cash flow, providing credit solutions, and managing payroll. Choose from business checking, small business loans, business credit cards, merchant services or visit our business resource center.

Investing by J.P. Morgan

Partner with a global leader who puts your financial needs first. Invest on your own or work with an advisor — we have the products, technology and investment education, to help you grow your wealth. Visit a J.P. Morgan Wealth Management Branch or check out our latest online investing features, offers, promotions, and coupons.

Community Reinvestment Act Public File</span></span></h1>
<p>JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. (JPMCB) is strongly committed to helping meet the financial needs of low- and moderate-income individuals and communities by providing loans, investments, and services across its banking markets. This commitment is part of our fundamental mission of providing quality financial services to existing and prospective customers in accordance with all applicable laws. This principle is embodied, in part, by the Community Reinvestment Act (CRA), which is a United States federal law intended to encourage all financial institutions to meet the credit needs of their communities, including low- and moderate- income areas, consistent with the institution's business strategies and safe and sound business practices.</p>
<p> </p>
<p>In accordance with the CRA regulation, JPMCB is required to maintain and, upon request, make available for public inspection a complete CRA Public File, which includes information about the bank's branch and ATM locations, products and services, regulatory performance evaluations of the bank’s record of meeting community credit needs, and other information.</p>
<p> </p>
<h2><span class="mds-title-large-heavier"><span class="cux-padding-16">Community Reinvestment Act Performance Evaluation</span></span></h2>
<p>JPMCB achieved an Outstanding rating from the Office of Comptroller and Currency (OCC) for the most recent performance evaluation, which covers January 1, 2020 to December 31, 2023. The full JPMCB CRA Performance Evaluation is available here: <a rel="noopener" class="chaseanalytics-opt-doc-dnld regular-link" href="/content/dam/chase-ux/documents/digital/resources/jpmcb-2024-community-reinvestment-act-performance-evaluation-03-11-2024.pdf" target="_blank">JPMCB CRA Performance Evaluation 2020-2023 (PDF)</a></p>
<p> </p>

<p> </p>

<h2><span class="mds-title-large-heavier"><span class="cux-padding-16">Written Comments from the Public</span></span></h2>
<p><a rel="noopener" class="chaseanalytics-opt-doc-dnld regular-link" data-pt-name="pdf_public-comments" href="/content/dam/chase-ux/documents/digital/resources/list_of_public_comments.pdf" target="_blank">List of public comments that specifically relate to the bank's performance in helping to meet community credit needs for the current and prior two years (PDF)</a></p>
<p> </p>
<h2><span class="mds-title-large-heavier"><span class="cux-padding-16">CRA Disclosure Statements</span></span></h2>
<p>JPMCB CRA Disclosure Statements are available for review at the Federal Financial Institution Examination Council (FFIEC) website: <a rel="noopener" class="chaseanalytics-opt-exlnk regular-link" data-pt-name="exit_ffiec-craadweb" href="https://www.ffiec.gov/data/cra/disclosure-reports" target="_blank">https://www.ffiec.gov/data/cra/disclosure-reports</a></p>
<p> </p>
<p>To view the Disclosure Statement, follow the link and select the year you wish to review, then enter “JPMorgan Chase Bank” in the Institution Name field.</p>
<p> </p>
<h2><span class="mds-title-large-heavier"><span class="cux-padding-16">HMDA Disclosure Statements</span></span></h2>
<p>JPMCB HMDA Disclosure Statements are available for review at the Federal Financial Institution Examination Council (FFIEC) Home Mortgage Disclosure Act website: <a rel="noopener" class="chaseanalytics-opt-exlnk regular-link" data-pt-name="exit_cfpb-reports" href="https://ffiec.cfpb.gov/data-publication/disclosure-reports" target="_blank">https://ffiec.cfpb.gov/data-publication/disclosure-reports</a></p>
<p> </p>
<p>To view the Disclosure Statement, follow the link and select the year you wish to review, enter “JPMorgan Chase Bank” in the Search by Institution Name field, then select the location you wish to review from the available MSA/MD section.</p>
<p> </p>
<h2><span class="mds-title-large-heavier"><span class="cux-padding-16">CRA Public File Requests</span></span></h2>
<p>If you would like to receive copy of the JPMCB CRA Public File, please complete and return a <a rel="noopener" class="chaseanalytics-opt-doc-dnld regular-link" data-pt-name="pdf_request-from-1" href="/content/dam/chase-ux/documents/digital/resources/cra_public_file_request_form.pdf" target="_blank">request form (PDF)</a> to <a class="chaseanalytics-track-link regular-link  click-to-call" data-pt-name="email_cra-public" href="mailto:cra.public.comments@chase.com">cra.public.comments@chase.com</a></p>
<p> </p>
<p>If you need assistance with any other matter, please visit Chase’s Complaints & Feedback website for contact information: <a href="/digital/resources/complaints-feedback" title="Follow link" class="chaseanalytics-track-link regular-link" data-pt-name="dg_feedback">https://www.chase.com/digital/resources/complaints-feedback</a></p>

JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. Community Reinvestment Act Public File JPMorgan Chase Bank, N.A. (JPMCB) is strongly committed to helping meet the financial needs of low- and moderate-income individuals and communities by providing loans, investments, and services across its banking markets. This commitment is part of our fundamental mission of providing quality financial services to existing and prospective customers in accordance with all applicable laws. This principle is embodied, in part, by the Community Reinvestment Act (CRA), which is a United States federal law intended to encourage all financial institutions to meet the credit needs of their communities, including low- and moderate- income areas, consistent with the institution's business strategies and safe and sound business practices.   In accordance with the CRA regulation, JPMCB is required to maintain and, upon request, make available for public inspection a complete CRA Public File, which includes information about the bank's branch and ATM locations, products and services, regulatory performance evaluations of the bank’s record of meeting community credit needs, and other information.   Community Reinvestment Act Performance Evaluation JPMCB achieved an Outstanding rating from the Office of Comptroller and Currency (OCC) for the most recent performance evaluation, which covers January 1, 2020 to December 31, 2023. The full JPMCB CRA Performance Evaluation is available here: JPMCB CRA Performance Evaluation 2020-2023 (PDF)   Information about JPMCB Branches General products and services offered at branches (PDF) List of JPMCB branches, including address and hours of operation (PDF) List of JPMCB branch openings and closings for the current and prior two years (PDF) JPMCB Branches Locator   JPMCB CRA Assessment Areas (AA) CRA AA List and AA Maps (PDF) List of census tracts included in JPMCB CRA AAs (PDF)   Written Comments from the Public List of public comments that specifically relate to the bank's performance in helping to meet community credit needs for the current and prior two years (PDF)   CRA Disclosure Statements JPMCB CRA Disclosure Statements are available for review at the Federal Financial Institution Examination Council (FFIEC) website: https://www.ffiec.gov/data/cra/disclosure-reports   To view the Disclosure Statement, follow the link and select the year you wish to review, then enter “JPMorgan Chase Bank” in the Institution Name field.   HMDA Disclosure Statements JPMCB HMDA Disclosure Statements are available for review at the Federal Financial Institution Examination Council (FFIEC) Home Mortgage Disclosure Act website: https://ffiec.cfpb.gov/data-publication/disclosure-reports   To view the Disclosure Statement, follow the link and select the year you wish to review, enter “JPMorgan Chase Bank” in the Search by Institution Name field, then select the location you wish to review from the available MSA/MD section.   CRA Public File Requests If you would like to receive copy of the JPMCB CRA Public File, please complete and return a request form (PDF) to cra.public.comments@chase.com   If you need assistance with any other matter, please visit Chase’s Complaints & Feedback website for contact information:  https://www.chase.com/digital/resources/complaints-feedback Checking Accounts Choose the checking account that works best for you. See our Chase Total Checking ® offer for new customers. Make purchases with your debit card, and bank from almost anywhere by phone, tablet or computer and more than 14,000 ATMs and 5,000 branches. Savings Accounts & CDs It’s never too early to begin saving. Open a savings account or open a Certificate of Deposit ( see interest rates ) and start saving your money. Credit Cards Chase credit cards  can help you buy the things you need. Many of our cards  offer rewards that can be redeemed for cash back  or travel-related perks. With so many options, it can be easy to find a card that matches your lifestyle. Plus, with Credit Journey you can get a  free credit score ! Mortgages & Home Equity Buy a home , refinance or put your home's equity to work with a cash-out refinance or home equity line of credit (HELOC) . View today's mortgage rates , use our mortgage calculator , and visit our Education Center for helpful tips. Start your mortgage preapproval online. Auto Chase Auto is here to help you get the right car. Apply for auto financing for a new or used car with Chase. Use the payment calculator to estimate monthly payments. Check out the Chase Auto Education Center to get car guidance from a trusted source. Chase for Business With Chase for Business you’ll receive all-in-one services and guidance from a team of business professionals. Explore  business checking , simplify payments acceptance with  merchant services , and consider  small business loans  or  business credit cards  for help with growth. You can also visit our business resource center . Sports & Entertainment Chase gives you access to unique sports, entertainment and culinary events through Chase Experiences and our exclusive partnerships such as the US Open , Madison Square Garden and Chase Center . Chase Security Center Our suite of security features can help you protect your info, money and give you peace of mind. See how we're dedicated to helping protect you , your accounts and your loved ones from financial abuse . Also, learn about the common tricks scammers are using to help you stay one step ahead of them. If you see unauthorized charges or believe your account was compromised contact us right away to report fraud . About Chase Chase serves millions of people with a broad range of products. Chase online lets you manage your Chase accounts, view statements, monitor activity, pay bills or transfer funds securely from one central place. To learn more, visit the Banking Education Center . For questions or concerns, please contact Chase customer service or let us know about Chase complaints and feedback . View the Chase Community Reinvestment Act Public File for the bank’s latest CRA rating and other CRA-related information. Investing by J.P. Morgan Partner with a global leader who puts your financial needs first. Invest on your own or work with an advisor  — we have the products , technology and investment education , to help you grow your wealth. Visit a J.P. Morgan Wealth Management Branch or check out our latest online investing features , offers, promotions, and coupons . data-feature="basic-text" class="mds-container"><div class="mds-row"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="Background__DefaultStyle-sc-o56u0b-1 Background__NeutralBackground-sc-o56u0b-4 fuhlfO ddsMYX mds-px-4 mds-px-at-768-0"><div class="BasicText__DropCap-sc-t3agr1-0"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 boMkaX"><p> </p>
<h2 style="text-align: center;"><span class="mds-title-xlarge">Watch out for scammers on social media</span></h2>
<p> </p>
<p style="text-align: center;">Scammers create listings on social media marketplaces offering merchandise at great prices. They’ll often ask you to pay <span style="text-align: left;">with Zelle<sup>®</sup>, checks, wires and crypto. In the end, they disappear — taking your money with them.</span></p>
<p style="text-align: center;"> </p>
</div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div><div class="WithSectionIdentifier__StyledSectionIdentifierDiv-sc-w1dr2r-0 hKRxwV w-100 h-100" data-testid="section-mapping" id="social-media-market-text" tabindex="-1"><div data-feature="structured-text" class="mds-container"><div class="mds-row"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="Background__DefaultStyle-sc-o56u0b-1 Background__PrimaryBackground-sc-o56u0b-2 fuhlfO bzLCuV"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="StructuredText__ImagePosition-sc-g71ha1-7 ctwurL"></div></div></div><div class="mds-jc-center mds-pb-6 mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12 mds-col-at-992-6"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col"><div class="StructuredText__TitleWrapper-sc-g71ha1-2 gOoBnv"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 gdoRDP"><h3><span class="mds-title-xlarge-heavier">How it can happen:</span></h3>
</div></div><div class="StructuredText__CrossPromoImagePadding-sc-g71ha1-6 kLzFFG"><div class="StructuredText__CrossPromoMediaInnerWrapper-sc-g71ha1-5 iYoLPP"><picture class="ImageWithSources__StyledPicture-sc-rc01gv-0 hIeuvF"><source srcSet="/content/dam/chase-ux/structured-text/personal/privacy-security/social-media-marketplace-scam.png" media=""/><img src="/content/dam/chase-ux/structured-text/personal/privacy-security/social-media-marketplace-scam.png" alt="" loading="eager" class="Image__Img-sc-qsmt06-0 hGVAqr mds-va-bottom w-100"/></picture></div></div></div></div></div><div class="mds-col-12 mds-col-at-992-6"><div class="mds-px-4 mds-px-at-768-5 mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="StructuredText__ColumnWithBorder-sc-g71ha1-0 dxHbJB mds-pl-5"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 gdoRDP"><h4><p><strong></strong><img src="/content/dam/unified-assets/illustration/chase-spot-illustrations/communication-chat-bubble/mds_ill_communication_chat_bubble_linear.svg" alt="a chat on social media marketplace scams"> <span class="mds-title-large-heavier">I thought I’d hit the jackpot</span></p>
</h4>
<p> </p>
<p>I really didn’t believe I could be so lucky when I saw a marketplace listing for the exact phone I’d been looking for. It was brand new and the price was so low, I thought it might be a scam. But when I messaged the seller, they told me it was an unwanted gift and they just wanted to get rid of it quickly. They even sent me pictures of the unopened box.</p>
<p> </p>
<p>I felt a little uneasy when they made excuses about why they couldn’t meet in person and insisted that Zelle<sup>®</sup> would be the easiest and quickest way to make the payment. They reassured me they’d ship it as soon as they got the money. The deal was so good and I didn’t want to miss out, so I sent it.</p>
<p> </p>
<p>I waited for weeks, but the phone never showed up. The seller had disappeared.</p>
<p> </p>
<h4>I wish I’d known:</h4>
<ul>
<li>Zelle<sup>®</sup> is for family, friends and businesses you know and trust, not for marketplace strangers.</li>
<li>Treat Zelle<sup>®</sup>, checks, wires, cashier’s checks, transfers, gift cards and crypto like cash. Once scammers get the money, you probably won’t get it back.</li>
<li>Scammers are advertising on social media and social marketplaces. Whenever possible, shop through official websites and be cautious of deals that seem too good to be true before sending any money.</li>
</ul>
<h4>Additional tip:</h4>
<ul>
<li>Scammers can make caller ID, emails and texts display as messages from your bank or other businesses. If you are ever unsure, end the conversation and reach out to the company directly through their official website.</li>
</ul>
</div><div class="StructuredText__SectionPadding-sc-g71ha1-3 iRNkXm"></div></div></div><div class="mds-pr-0 mds-row mds-no-gutters"></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></section><section aria-labelledby="tab-Home services" aria-hidden="true"><div id="1" class="mds-d-none"><div class="HorizontalTab__TabPanelWrapper-sc-w4jzmm-2 kSazWq"><div><div data-feature="basic-text" class="mds-container"><div class="mds-row"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="Background__DefaultStyle-sc-o56u0b-1 Background__NeutralBackground-sc-o56u0b-4 fuhlfO ddsMYX Background__BackgroundWithBorderRadius-sc-o56u0b-0"><div class="BasicText__MainContainer-sc-t3agr1-1 knhfJf mds-jc-center mds-no-gutters mds-row"><div class="mds-text-break mds-col mds-col-at-768-10 mds-px-4 mds-px-at-768-0"><div class="BasicText__DropCap-sc-t3agr1-0"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 boMkaX"><p> </p>
<h2 style="text-align: center;"><span class="mds-title-xlarge">Watch out for social media ads for household services</span></h2>
<p> </p>
<p style="text-align: center;">Scammers advertise services like house cleaning, home repairs or installations at low prices on social media marketplaces. But when you book, they ask for a deposit using a payment app like Zelle<sup>®</sup> or a wire transfer. Then they never turn up and disappear with your money.</p>
<p> </p>
</div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div><div class="WithSectionIdentifier__StyledSectionIdentifierDiv-sc-w1dr2r-0 hKRxwV w-100 h-100" data-testid="section-mapping" id="home-services" tabindex="-1"><div data-feature="structured-text" class="mds-container"><div class="mds-row"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="Background__DefaultStyle-sc-o56u0b-1 Background__PrimaryBackground-sc-o56u0b-2 fuhlfO bzLCuV"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="StructuredText__ImagePosition-sc-g71ha1-7 ctwurL"></div></div></div><div class="mds-jc-center mds-pb-6 mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12 mds-col-at-992-6"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col"><div class="StructuredText__TitleWrapper-sc-g71ha1-2 gOoBnv"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 gdoRDP"><h3><span class="mds-title-xlarge-heavier">How it can happen:</span></h3>
</div></div><div class="StructuredText__CrossPromoImagePadding-sc-g71ha1-6 kLzFFG"><div class="StructuredText__CrossPromoMediaInnerWrapper-sc-g71ha1-5 iYoLPP"><picture class="ImageWithSources__StyledPicture-sc-rc01gv-0 hIeuvF"><source srcSet="/content/dam/chase-ux/structured-text/personal/privacy-security/home-services-scams.jpg" media=""/><img src="/content/dam/chase-ux/structured-text/personal/privacy-security/home-services-scams.jpg" alt="" loading="eager" class="Image__Img-sc-qsmt06-0 hGVAqr mds-va-bottom w-100"/></picture></div></div></div></div></div><div class="mds-col-12 mds-col-at-992-6"><div class="mds-px-4 mds-px-at-768-5 mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="StructuredText__ColumnWithBorder-sc-g71ha1-0 dxHbJB mds-pl-5"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 gdoRDP"><h4>Social media ads</h4>
<p>I’d been looking for a house cleaner when an ad appeared in my social feed for a cleaning company with a really good oﬀer for ﬁrst-time customers. I clicked on the ad and it took me to a professional looking website with good reviews and the cleaner's contact information. I reached out to the cleaner and they had a special discount if I wired them a deposit for the first six cleanings, which I did. But no one turned up and the company never responded to my complaint. I wired the money so the cleaner had received the money right away. Then they just disappeared and I couldn't get my money back.</p>
<p> </p>
<h4>Social media marketplaces</h4>
<p>I needed a new boiler and saw a plumber advertising their services on a social media marketplace. When I clicked the link, it opened messenger and we texted back and forth about prices and some questions about the job. The plumber was very responsive and seemed to know his stuﬀ. We agreed on a price so he booked me a time and date for the install. It was a big job so I wasn’t surprised he asked for half up front. He gave me his Zelle<sup>®</sup> info and I sent the deposit. A few days later I tried to conﬁrm the appointment and got no response. I never heard from them again and no one turned up. I sent the money with Zelle<sup>®</sup> so he received the money right away. Then he disappeared, so I couldn’t get my money back.</p>
<p> </p>
<h4>Help protect yourself</h4>
<ul>
<li>Before you book any household job, read the reviews, check references and meet them in person.</li>
<li>Get multiple written estimates from diﬀerent companies and only hire licensed contractors. </li>
<li>Never pay a deposit using a payment app like Zelle<sup>® </sup>or a wire transfer. Both are like giving someone cash. Once you send the money, it’s unlikely you’ll be able to get it back.</li>
</ul>
</div><div class="StructuredText__SectionPadding-sc-g71ha1-3 iRNkXm"></div></div></div><div class="mds-pr-0 mds-row mds-no-gutters"></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></section><section aria-labelledby="tab-Company Impersonation scams" aria-hidden="true"><div id="2" class="mds-d-none"><div class="HorizontalTab__TabPanelWrapper-sc-w4jzmm-2 kSazWq"><div><div class="WithSectionIdentifier__StyledSectionIdentifierDiv-sc-w1dr2r-0 hKRxwV w-100 h-100" data-testid="section-mapping" id="knowncompany" tabindex="-1"><div data-feature="basic-text" class="mds-container"><div class="mds-row"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="Background__DefaultStyle-sc-o56u0b-1 Background__NeutralBackground-sc-o56u0b-4 fuhlfO ddsMYX Background__BackgroundWithBorderRadius-sc-o56u0b-0"><div class="BasicText__MainContainer-sc-t3agr1-1 knhfJf mds-jc-center mds-no-gutters mds-row"><div class="mds-text-break mds-col mds-col-at-768-10 mds-px-4 mds-px-at-768-0"><div class="BasicText__DropCap-sc-t3agr1-0"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 boMkaX"><p> </p>
<h2 style="text-align: center;"><b><span class="mds-title-xlarge">Watch out for scammers impersonating Chase</span></b></h2>
<p> </p>
<p style="text-align: center;">They’ll pretend there’s an issue with your account and your money is at risk. They may claim there’s fraud on your account <span style="text-align: left;">and put pressure on you to act fast so you don’t lose the rest of your money.</span></p>
<p style="text-align: center;"> </p>
</div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div><div class="WithSectionIdentifier__StyledSectionIdentifierDiv-sc-w1dr2r-0 hKRxwV w-100 h-100" data-testid="section-mapping" id="known-company-text" tabindex="-1"><div data-feature="structured-text" class="mds-container"><div class="mds-row"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="Background__DefaultStyle-sc-o56u0b-1 Background__PrimaryBackground-sc-o56u0b-2 fuhlfO bzLCuV"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="StructuredText__ImagePosition-sc-g71ha1-7 ctwurL"></div></div></div><div class="mds-jc-center mds-pb-6 mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12 mds-col-at-992-6"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col"><div class="StructuredText__TitleWrapper-sc-g71ha1-2 gOoBnv"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 gdoRDP"><h3><span class="mds-title-xlarge-heavier">How it can happen:</span></h3>
</div></div><div class="StructuredText__CrossPromoImagePadding-sc-g71ha1-6 kLzFFG"><div class="StructuredText__CrossPromoMediaInnerWrapper-sc-g71ha1-5 iYoLPP"><picture class="ImageWithSources__StyledPicture-sc-rc01gv-0 hIeuvF"><source srcSet="/content/dam/chase-ux/structured-text/personal/privacy-security/chase-company-impersonation-scams.png" media=""/><img src="/content/dam/chase-ux/structured-text/personal/privacy-security/chase-company-impersonation-scams.png" alt="" loading="eager" class="Image__Img-sc-qsmt06-0 hGVAqr mds-va-bottom w-100"/></picture></div></div></div></div></div><div class="mds-col-12 mds-col-at-992-6"><div class="mds-px-4 mds-px-at-768-5 mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="StructuredText__ColumnWithBorder-sc-g71ha1-0 dxHbJB mds-pl-5"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 gdoRDP"><h4><p><strong></strong><img src="/content/dam/unified-assets/illustration/chase-spot-illustrations/communication-chat-bubble/mds_ill_communication_chat_bubble_linear.svg" alt="a chat on company impersonation scams"> <span class="mds-title-large-heavier">My phone rang. It said it was from Chase.</span></p>
</h4>
<p> </p>
<p>The man on the line spoke calmly and asked if I had withdrawn $2,200 from my account. When I told him it wasn’t me, he said I needed to transfer my money to a secure Chase account that the fraud department had created in my name.</p>
<p> </p>
<p>I was scared it was a scam, but everything sounded official. When I hesitated, he reassured me and offered to connect me with his supervisor. The woman was also professional and nice. She said, “We’re trying to help you. I’m watching activity in your account right now. If we don’t move fast, you could lose everything.” When I said I felt more comfortable going to the Chase branch, she confided in me that they suspected branch employees may be in on it. So, I went ahead and transferred the money to the new account.</p>
<p> </p>
<p>After I hung up, doubt crept in. I called the number on the back of my card. My voice shook as the Chase employee told me my account had been emptied and there was no other account in my name. They couldn’t get the money back because I transferred the money to the scammer and it was sent almost instantaneously.</p>
<p> </p>
<h4>I wish I’d known:</h4>
<ul>
<li>Scammers impersonate banks and claim your account is at risk. Reputable banks will never ask you to move money to resolve fraud.</li>
<li>Scammers can make caller ID, emails and texts display as messages from your bank or other businesses. If you are ever unsure, end the conversation and reach out to the company directly through their official website.</li>
<li>Scammers may urge you to distrust bank employees, but neither your bank nor the police will ask you to help in a sting operation.</li>
<li>I should treat Zelle<sup>®</sup>, checks, wires, cashier’s checks, gift cards, transfers and crypto like cash. Once scammers get the money, you probably won’t get it back.</li>
</ul>
<p> </p>
<h4>Additional tip:</h4>
<ul>
<li>Scammers are advertising on social media and social marketplaces. Whenever possible, shop through official websites and be cautious of deals that seem too good to be true before sending any money.</li>
</ul>
</div><div class="StructuredText__SectionPadding-sc-g71ha1-3 iRNkXm"></div></div></div><div class="mds-pr-0 mds-row mds-no-gutters"></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></section><section aria-labelledby="tab-Fake listings & property rental scams" aria-hidden="true"><div id="3" class="mds-d-none"><div class="HorizontalTab__TabPanelWrapper-sc-w4jzmm-2 kSazWq"><div><div data-feature="basic-text" class="mds-container"><div class="mds-row"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="Background__DefaultStyle-sc-o56u0b-1 Background__NeutralBackground-sc-o56u0b-4 fuhlfO ddsMYX Background__BackgroundWithBorderRadius-sc-o56u0b-0"><div class="BasicText__MainContainer-sc-t3agr1-1 knhfJf mds-jc-center mds-no-gutters mds-row"><div class="mds-text-break mds-col mds-col-at-768-10 mds-px-4 mds-px-at-768-0"><div class="BasicText__DropCap-sc-t3agr1-0"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 boMkaX"><p> </p>
<h2 style="text-align: center;"><span class="mds-title-xlarge">Watch out for vacation rental and real estate scams</span></h2>
<p> </p>
<p style="text-align: center;">Scammers are posing as real estate agents and posting fake listings on vacation sites, looking to sell or rent a home that doesn’t exist. They’ll often pressure you into sending a ‘deposit’ to hold the property, saying there’s a lot of demand for it.</p>
<p> </p>
</div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div><div class="WithSectionIdentifier__StyledSectionIdentifierDiv-sc-w1dr2r-0 hKRxwV w-100 h-100" data-testid="section-mapping" id="fake-listings-text" tabindex="-1"><div data-feature="structured-text" class="mds-container"><div class="mds-row"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="Background__DefaultStyle-sc-o56u0b-1 Background__PrimaryBackground-sc-o56u0b-2 fuhlfO bzLCuV"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="StructuredText__ImagePosition-sc-g71ha1-7 ctwurL"></div></div></div><div class="mds-jc-center mds-pb-6 mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12 mds-col-at-992-6"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col"><div class="StructuredText__TitleWrapper-sc-g71ha1-2 gOoBnv"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 gdoRDP"><h3><span class="mds-title-xlarge-heavier">How it can happen:</span></h3>
</div></div><div class="StructuredText__CrossPromoImagePadding-sc-g71ha1-6 kLzFFG"><div class="StructuredText__CrossPromoMediaInnerWrapper-sc-g71ha1-5 iYoLPP"><picture class="ImageWithSources__StyledPicture-sc-rc01gv-0 hIeuvF"><source srcSet="/content/dam/chase-ux/structured-text/personal/privacy-security/fake-listings-scams.jpg" media=""/><img src="/content/dam/chase-ux/structured-text/personal/privacy-security/fake-listings-scams.jpg" alt="" loading="eager" class="Image__Img-sc-qsmt06-0 hGVAqr mds-va-bottom w-100"/></picture></div></div></div></div></div><div class="mds-col-12 mds-col-at-992-6"><div class="mds-px-4 mds-px-at-768-5 mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="StructuredText__ColumnWithBorder-sc-g71ha1-0 dxHbJB mds-pl-5"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 gdoRDP"><p>We’re a group on a tight budget, but we decide to splurge a bit. We found a great house on a major vacation rental website and emailed through the website. A man called us from his cell and was really nice. Since we were a group, he even said we could each pay our share of the deposit using Zelle<sup>®</sup> or a digital payment app. So, we each sent our share for the deposit, and later our shares for the balance.</p>
<p> </p>
<p>As the trip date got closer, we called the guy to make sure everything was all set, but couldn’t get a hold of him. We emailed through the vacation rental but the guy who responded said he didn’t have our reservation and he had a different phone number. I called him in a panic, and he said he was the legitimate owner but that someone had copied his listing, right down to the exact wording. The legitimate owner said he’d reported the fake listing several times, but it still wasn’t taken down. We contacted the vacation rental website, but they said since we hadn’t paid through the site, their guarantee against fake listings did not apply.</p>
<p> </p>
<h4>Help protect yourself</h4>
<p> </p>
<p>Most major property rental sites offer fraud guarantees, but only if you pay and communicate with the owners through the site. <strong>Try to see properties in person and avoid sending deposits through wire transfers or digital payments like Zelle<sup>®</sup> since that’s like sending cash and once you send it you may not be able to get it back.</strong></p>
</div><div class="StructuredText__SectionPadding-sc-g71ha1-3 iRNkXm"></div></div></div><div class="mds-pr-0 mds-row mds-no-gutters"></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></section><section aria-labelledby="tab-Police & government scams" aria-hidden="true"><div id="4" class="mds-d-none"><div class="HorizontalTab__TabPanelWrapper-sc-w4jzmm-2 kSazWq"><div><div data-feature="basic-text" class="mds-container"><div class="mds-row"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="Background__DefaultStyle-sc-o56u0b-1 Background__NeutralBackground-sc-o56u0b-4 fuhlfO ddsMYX Background__BackgroundWithBorderRadius-sc-o56u0b-0"><div class="BasicText__MainContainer-sc-t3agr1-1 knhfJf mds-jc-center mds-no-gutters mds-row"><div class="mds-text-break mds-col mds-col-at-768-10 mds-px-4 mds-px-at-768-0"><div class="BasicText__DropCap-sc-t3agr1-0"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 boMkaX"><p> </p>
<h2 style="text-align: center;"><span class="mds-title-xlarge">Scammers are impersonating government officials</span></h2>
<p style="text-align: center;">Scammers often pose as representatives from agencies such as the IRS, FBI, police, immigration, or Social Security. They may use bits of your personal information to enhance their credibility. Their tactics can include offering services for a fee to help recover lost funds or using intimidation to coerce you into sending money.</p>
<p> </p>
</div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div><div class="WithSectionIdentifier__StyledSectionIdentifierDiv-sc-w1dr2r-0 hKRxwV w-100 h-100" data-testid="section-mapping" id="police-government-text" tabindex="-1"><div data-feature="structured-text" class="mds-container"><div class="mds-row"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="Background__DefaultStyle-sc-o56u0b-1 Background__PrimaryBackground-sc-o56u0b-2 fuhlfO bzLCuV"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="StructuredText__ImagePosition-sc-g71ha1-7 ctwurL"></div></div></div><div class="mds-jc-center mds-pb-6 mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12 mds-col-at-992-6"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col"><div class="StructuredText__TitleWrapper-sc-g71ha1-2 gOoBnv"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 gdoRDP"><h3><span class="mds-title-xlarge-heavier">How it can happen:</span></h3>
</div></div><div class="StructuredText__CrossPromoImagePadding-sc-g71ha1-6 kLzFFG"><div class="StructuredText__CrossPromoMediaInnerWrapper-sc-g71ha1-5 iYoLPP"><picture class="ImageWithSources__StyledPicture-sc-rc01gv-0 hIeuvF"><source srcSet="/content/dam/chase-ux/structured-text/personal/privacy-security/police-government-scams.jpg" media=""/><img src="/content/dam/chase-ux/structured-text/personal/privacy-security/police-government-scams.jpg" alt="" loading="eager" class="Image__Img-sc-qsmt06-0 hGVAqr mds-va-bottom w-100"/></picture></div></div></div></div></div><div class="mds-col-12 mds-col-at-992-6"><div class="mds-px-4 mds-px-at-768-5 mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="StructuredText__ColumnWithBorder-sc-g71ha1-0 dxHbJB mds-pl-5"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 gdoRDP"><h3><p><strong></strong><img src="/content/dam/unified-assets/illustration/chase-spot-illustrations/communication-chat-bubble/mds_ill_communication_chat_bubble_linear.svg" alt="a chat on government impersonation scams"> <span class="mds-title-large-heavier">Seeing “IRS” on my caller ID stopped me cold</span></p>
</h3>
<p> </p>
<p>It was a Washington D.C. number. I used a search engine and the number belonged to the IRS. When the woman said I owed a lot of money in unpaid taxes, my stomach dropped. She claimed they’d sent reminders and what I owed had been outstanding for weeks, so now I only had an hour to pay it all back or face a huge penalty.</p>
<p> </p>
<p>She knew my address, my employer and even the last four digits of my social security number. It was so convincing.</p>
<p> </p>
<p>I wired $1,500 thinking things would be settled. An hour later, when the fear wore off, I called the IRS myself. They told me I’d been scammed, they would never demand immediate payment in that way. I had underestimated how advanced these scams could get.</p>
<p> </p>
<h3>I wish I’d known:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Scammers are able to make caller ID appear as if the call is coming from the IRS or another legitimate business.</li>
<li>Data breaches make it easy for scammers to access my personal information.</li>
<li>Before sending money, I should’ve hung up and called the agency directly to confirm.</li>
<li>The way you pay matters. I should treat Zelle<sup>®</sup>, checks, wires, cashierʼs checks, gift cards, transfers and crypto like cash. Once scammers get the money, you probably won’t get it back.</li>
<li>The IRS typically contacts you for the first time by mail. To confirm it’s really them, the IRS recommends logging on to your IRS online account to see if there is a letter or notice on your profile.</li>
</ul>
<h3>Additional tip:</h3>
<ul>
<li>Scammers are advertising on social media and social marketplaces. Whenever possible, shop through official websites and be cautious of deals that seem too good to be true before sending any money.</li>
</ul>
</div><div class="StructuredText__SectionPadding-sc-g71ha1-3 iRNkXm"></div></div></div><div class="mds-pr-0 mds-row mds-no-gutters"></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></section><section aria-labelledby="tab-Pets" aria-hidden="true"><div id="5" class="mds-d-none"><div class="HorizontalTab__TabPanelWrapper-sc-w4jzmm-2 kSazWq"><div><div class="WithSectionIdentifier__StyledSectionIdentifierDiv-sc-w1dr2r-0 hKRxwV w-100 h-100" data-testid="section-mapping" id="pets-text" tabindex="-1"><div data-feature="basic-text" class="mds-container"><div class="mds-row"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="Background__DefaultStyle-sc-o56u0b-1 Background__NeutralBackground-sc-o56u0b-4 fuhlfO ddsMYX Background__BackgroundWithBorderRadius-sc-o56u0b-0"><div class="BasicText__MainContainer-sc-t3agr1-1 knhfJf mds-jc-center mds-no-gutters mds-row"><div class="mds-text-break mds-col mds-col-at-768-10 mds-px-4 mds-px-at-768-0"><div class="BasicText__DropCap-sc-t3agr1-0"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 boMkaX"><p> </p>
<h2 style="text-align: center;"><span class="mds-title-xlarge">Watch out for irresistible cuteness</span></h2>
<p> </p>
<p style="text-align: center;">Scammers advertise adorable looking pets for sale that don’t exist. They often instill a sense of urgency by asking you to pay a deposit to secure the animal before someone else does. But then they either disappear or keep asking you for more money to “cover new costs.”</p>
<p> </p>
</div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div></div><div><div class="WithSectionIdentifier__StyledSectionIdentifierDiv-sc-w1dr2r-0 hKRxwV w-100 h-100" data-testid="section-mapping" id="pets-structured-text" tabindex="-1"><div data-feature="structured-text" class="mds-container"><div class="mds-row"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="Background__DefaultStyle-sc-o56u0b-1 Background__PrimaryBackground-sc-o56u0b-2 fuhlfO bzLCuV"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="StructuredText__ImagePosition-sc-g71ha1-7 ctwurL"></div></div></div><div class="mds-jc-center mds-pb-6 mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col-12 mds-col-at-992-6"><div class="mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="mds-col"><div class="StructuredText__TitleWrapper-sc-g71ha1-2 gOoBnv"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 gdoRDP"><h3><span class="mds-title-xlarge-heavier">How it can happen:</span></h3>
</div></div><div class="StructuredText__CrossPromoImagePadding-sc-g71ha1-6 kLzFFG"><div class="StructuredText__CrossPromoMediaInnerWrapper-sc-g71ha1-5 iYoLPP"><picture class="ImageWithSources__StyledPicture-sc-rc01gv-0 hIeuvF"><source srcSet="/content/dam/chase-ux/structured-text/personal/privacy-security/pets-scams.jpg" media=""/><img src="/content/dam/chase-ux/structured-text/personal/privacy-security/pets-scams.jpg" alt="" loading="eager" class="Image__Img-sc-qsmt06-0 hGVAqr mds-va-bottom w-100"/></picture></div></div></div></div></div><div class="mds-col-12 mds-col-at-992-6"><div class="mds-px-4 mds-px-at-768-5 mds-row mds-no-gutters"><div class="StructuredText__ColumnWithBorder-sc-g71ha1-0 dxHbJB mds-pl-5"><div class="security__TextColor-sc-1pgztkc-0 gdoRDP"><p>After our elderly dog passed away, my husband’s health deteriorated as he lost his cuddle buddy. So, I decided to surprise him with a new puppy. I found the perfect little dog online and contacted the "breeder." They told me the puppy would be available in a few weeks, but they could reserve her for me with a small deposit. I paid it happily and relaxed.</p>
<p> </p>
<p>But then things got complicated. First the "breeder" got in touch to say there was a problem with the payment and I needed to send another deposit. A day later there was a quarantine fee. Then a permit fee. I thought it was normal, so I went out and bought dog food and toys in preparation. But when the seller wanted another payment I complained, only to be threatened with a lawsuit for "puppy abandonment." </p>
<p> </p>
<p>At that point I called the police to be told there was no such law, the so-called breeder was really a criminal, and I couldn’t get my money back.</p>
<p> </p>
<h4>Help protect yourself</h4>
<ul>
<li>Do your homework—research the breeder and their reviews.</li>
<li>Don’t send any payments or share personal information until you’ve seen the pet in person ﬁrst.</li>
</ul>
